title.en: ei, jeg, -ig, o, y and ø — and whose pronunciation this is

explanation.short: Norwegian has no official spoken standard: only the spelling is regulated, and people speak in their own regional ways. Go uses one Eastern (Oslo-area) pronunciation as a reference, not as the only right one. In it, ei is like "ay" in "hay" (hei), the ending -eg is said "-ai" (jeg is YAI), the g in -ig and -lig is silent (hyggelig ends in -lee), o is often like "oo" in "moon" (broren) and ø is like the vowel in "fur", with rounded lips (søstera).
explanation.more: u is a rounded "ee" (hus, du) and y is like the German ü (hyggelig): neither is an English sound. A short o before a double consonant is more like English "o" in "off" (kopp). Regional speech differs a good deal (r, the melody, kj and sj), and those differences are normal Norwegian, not mistakes.

options: like the vowel in "fur", with rounded lips
